_note: Authored judgement. The rulings recorded in prose in docs/curation.md, expressed as data so the browse view can apply them. Justin edits this; nothing generates it. Counts under 'expect' are assertions - tools/gen_browse.py checks every one and reports mismatches rather than silently drifting.

_provenance_values.justin: Justin ruled on it, against a rendered sheet
_provenance_values.visual: Claude ruled on it by looking, and Justin has not seen it
_provenance_values.reconstructed: docs/curation.md states the ruling but not its members; this is a pattern fitted to the prose, and it may be wrong
_provenance_values.rule: no ruling exists; the mechanical pass proposed it

drop_groups.reason: script digits; no other script's general numerics were kept

_drop_blocks_why: The blocks behind the dropped groups. A shape rule claims glyphs by name, so a SignWriting circle sits in `circles` and an emoji circle in `circles` too, while their own group is dropped entire. docs/curation.md rules that dropped means dropped from the inventory, not merely deselected, so the block goes wherever it landed. This removes strays the group-by-group tally in that file never counted, so the totals here run slightly below it - deliberately, and reported separately.

regroup.why: the nine mahjong circle tiles were pulled out by the CIRCLE shape rule; they are a numbered suit
TETRAGRAM FOR FULL CIRCLE was pulled out by the CIRCLE shape rule

leaves.note: bare line primitives - a diagonal, a hook, a corner, an ellipse. Not script content in the ordinary sense.
docs/curation.md names the dropped categories but not their members. This pattern is fitted to that prose and has not been checked against the sheet Justin ruled from.
exemplars are ace of clubs and king of hearts - chosen for colour coverage, not as range bounds. See docs/curation.md.
characters, bamboos, circles - codepoint order is already the run order.
a combination enumeration - a 7x7 pip grid plus a back tile. Its ends are corners of the space, so four seeded-random exemplars stand in for it.
Tai Xuan Jing, ternary, 3^4. A combination enumeration: the first member is the degenerate all-solid one.
Yijing, binary, 2^6. Same reasoning as the tetragrams.
fragments of a picture split across cells - half running man, thirds of the pointing index, half folder. None is usable alone.
a combination enumeration - 2^6 less the four already in Block Elements.
docs/curation.md gives the count but not the members; this pattern is fitted to it.
General_Category Nl, so ID_Start and Alphabetic, and they case-map to the small forms. Not symbols in the sense the rest of the set is.
parked for later sorting rather than ruled on.

rulings._why: Exemplars are given by codepoint here rather than taken from the ends, because three of these families straddle two blocks: their missing members were encoded in Letterlike Symbols before the maths block existed, so the alphabetical last is not the numerical last. docs/curation.md states two of the pairs outright - double-struck capitals U+1D538 to U+2124, fraktur capitals U+1D504 to U+2128 - and they are reproduced exactly.

leaves.note: capitals and lowercase, pooled into one leaf. Caps lack B E F H I L M R and smalls lack e g o, which live in Letterlike Symbols.
the five borrowed capitals are named BLACK-LETTER, not FRAKTUR, which is why a naive stem match misses them.
the only one of the five with digits. Capitals lack C H N P Q R Z.
the 29 ASCII duplicates, identified by decomposing below U+0080; then fullwidth currency, fullwidth Latin-1 marks, halfwidth CJK punctuation.

pull_in.why: Five styled alphanumeric families from Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols. This revises the inventory rule, which excludes letters and digits of every script: first and last make a full alphabet run cost two exemplars, so the exception is cheap. The odd member counts are not an error - the missing members were encoded in Letterlike Symbols before the maths block existed, so three of these families straddle two blocks.
